title: Instruments and measurement
goal: Read a resistor's colour code, check it with the multimeter, and discover that the meter itself changes what it measures in a high-resistance circuit.
theory: Four colour bands give two digits, a multiplier and a tolerance: yellow-violet-red-gold is 47 × 10² Ω = 4.7 kΩ ±5 %, so any value from 4465 Ω to 4935 Ω is in spec.

A digital multimeter in a volt range is not invisible: it puts its input resistance (10 MΩ here) in parallel with whatever it touches. Across a 1 MΩ resistor that parallel combination is 909 kΩ, so a divider of two 1 MΩ resistors no longer splits the supply in half while the meter is connected. This is called loading.
Rule of thumb: the meter's resistance should be at least 100 times the resistance it is connected across.

prelab.label: Ideal voltage across the lower 1 MΩ of a 10 V divider
The same voltage with a 10 MΩ meter connected across it

procedure: Load the reference build (or build it): R1 alone on the board, and a divider of R2 and R3 (both 1 MΩ) across a 10 V supply.
Set multimeter M1 to Ω and touch its probes across R1 (the part must not be powered). Record the reading.
Set M2 to V and put it across R3. Press Run and record the reading.
Compare with your pre-lab values. Which of the two measurements is disturbed by the instrument, and why?
